recommendations.rationale: Defer (do not execute or select in this phase) a single bounded prediction_braking probe at one saved late projected state where the tip moved fastest, comparing the recorded input with an instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed 0.01 s horizon. This locally measures whether the recorded commands left endpoint speed reduction unused, which bears on the command/authority mechanism versus the objective-weighting mechanism.

Defer a local_comparison check that adopts exactly one weight change (for example terminal tip-speed weighting) at a saved state whose effective horizon matches the authorized 0.01 s, since sampled late effective horizons of 1-5 intervals show matching is a real constraint. This is the only authorized operation that could locally separate objective weighting from solver early-stop effects, and it cannot establish closed-loop settling.

Defer any further progress on the solver-quality mechanism until the non-retained historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces are made available or a wider retained sample of updates is read; without them the early-stop and weighting hypotheses remain locally indistinguishable.

attribution.reason: Configuration gives zero weight to terminal and holding tip speed while position tracking carries weight 1.0, so the recorded plan objective is dominated by position; consistent with reach being achieved (error 0.0076 m) while terminal speed is still 0.6352 m/s. Raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions.

Nearly every update was stopped by policy (relative_seed_improvement / budget_best_feasible) with only 1 Solve_Succeeded, mean update wall time 17.0752 s against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled late effective horizons collapsing to 1 interval; such plans are plausibly under-damped and give the receding-horizon controller little lookahead in which to null tip velocity.

Sampled late requested tensions reach 7.9904 N and 7.9439 N on single channels of an inventory limit of 8.0 N per tendon, so braking/redirect authority may be bounded; the degree of binding (and whether it mattered) was not quantified in this phase.

The scheduling contract for this run states synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time; the 35 deadline misses and the 17.0752 s mean update wall time are compute overruns, not simulated-time stalls, so they cannot by themselves displace the tip. They remain relevant only as a symptom of solver load.

Retained matched-interval velocity and projected-state offsets show the projected GVS prediction is close to but not identical to the full serial-backend endpoint; a saved-state probe over a single 0.01 s horizon cannot explain an entire settling failure, and no retained evidence ranks this against the command-objective and solver-quality mechanisms.

facts.statement: The run passed terminal reach (reach_passed true; terminal tip error 0.0076426 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance; tolerance 0.01 m) but failed sampled settling: late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810 and late_max_error_m 0.0581381 both exceed the settling criteria (position 0.01 m, speed 0.02 m/s, window 0.05 s), and terminal tip speed 0.6352 m/s remains above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

34 of 35 controller updates ended with solver status User_Requested_Stop versus 1 Solve_Succeeded; sampled stopping reasons are 'relative_seed_improvement' (updates 30, 31) and 'budget_best_feasible' (update 32); mean update wall time is 17.0752 s; sampled late effective horizons are 10 (update 2), 5 (30), 4 (31), 3 (32) and 1 (34) control intervals.
Controller configuration sets terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, with tracking_weight 1.0, velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001.

Sampled requested tension commands reach 7.9904 N (update 30) and 7.9439 N (update 31) on individual channels; the retained evidence inventory lists a force limit of 8.0 N for each of the six tendons.
